responses.response: Keep the same baseline fields used by the workspace examples: $schema, name, title, include, and imageAliases. For projects/payments/likec4.config.json, keep include.paths pointing to ["../shared"] and keep imageAliases mapping "@" to "../shared/images/"; both paths are relative to the config file inside projects/payments, so they will not break imports. Do not replace ../shared or repoint @ if existing diagrams already depend on them; extend the config later by appending new shared sources and adding new aliases, not by rewriting the baseline.

Use the repository in two passes. First create the template baseline from projects/template/: split the 1200-line system.c4 into system-model.c4 for all model definitions and relationships, and system-views.c4 for all views. Then, once it grows, split like projects/spec-showcase/: actors-systems.c4 for actors, systems, and C1 relationships; containers.c4 for C2 containers and their relationships; components.c4 for C3 internals; context-views.c4 for C1 views; container-views.c4 for C2 views; and component-views.c4 for C3 views. Add deployment.c4 plus deployment-views.c4 when you introduce deployment nodes, and add use-case-views.c4 and operations-views.c4 for scenario and operational slices. Keep Use Cases, Deployment, and Operations as separate view files/categories; only create extra model files for them if they introduce new modeled elements rather than just alternate views.

To avoid breaking existing behavior, preserve the current include.paths order exactly as it is and append the new shared source after the existing entries so current source precedence does not change. Keep existing image alias keys and targets unchanged, especially any alias already used in diagrams. Give the new image root its own alias name instead of reusing or renaming an existing one. Use paths relative to the project's likec4.config.json, and if the new source contributes only images, add only a new imageAliases entry rather than rewriting existing include paths. In short: preserve order, preserve existing aliases, append new sources, and namespace new images with a fresh alias.

No, not by itself. This skill is enough for wiring a project's likec4.config.json so shared specs and images resolve correctly, but adding a second LikeC4 project is also a workspace-organization task. Pair it with organize-multi-project for project layout, shared-folder boundaries, and naming conventions. If the workspace is unfamiliar, an understand-project-structure pass is also useful before you add the new project.

Keep ../shared in place and append ../platform-shared after it in include.paths so the existing source ordering stays intact. In imageAliases, keep the current shared alias exactly as it is, for example "@": "../shared/images/", and add a second non-colliding alias for platform images such as "@platform": "../platform-shared/images/". Do not repoint @ to the platform folder and do not try to make both folders share the same alias. If the platform source currently expects a colliding alias name, rename only the new platform alias and update new references to use that new namespace.

Change only these parts and leave every other field untouched: {"include":{"paths":["../shared","../platform-shared"]},"imageAliases":{"@":"../shared/images/","@platform":"../platform-shared/images/"}}. This keeps existing @/... references working, appends the new shared source after the old one, and gives platform images their own alias so there is no collision.
